findings.body: The approved T1 seam requires malformed supported inputs to retain a stable envelope identity, raw payload and safe reason so they can be saved and eventually set aside (plans/MSG-1.md:91). This branch instead gives malformed classifications no event or reason. Storage also accepts only message/slash kinds and nonempty raw channels, so a malformed envelope with unknown scope cannot be represented or saved. Pin a distinct saveable malformed-event contract and prove its persistence separately from rejection of invalid repository inputs. This concerns T1's classifier/storage contract, not later runtime execution.
findings.title: Not done: durable malformed supported-input contract

findings.body: The shared seam explicitly requires a question_reply result containing the qualified reply candidate and ordinary-message fallback (plans/MSG-1.md:112). This union permits only ordinary messages or drops, and no InboundQuestionReply or durable-handler result is declared. NewMessage (apps/core/src/domain/types.ts:125) does not carry the bot-author identity and qualified question locator needed by that contract. Later codecs therefore cannot return the promised side-effect-free question candidate through the pinned boundary. Add these shared signatures here; durable answer execution and its owner test remain T11's responsibility.
findings.title: Not done: shared question-reply unpack contract

findings.body: The approved record contract requires an app foreign key (plans/MSG-1.md:99), but app_id is unconstrained text in both the schema and migration. The integration fixture creates no app rows before successfully saving inbox-app and other-app events, demonstrating that raw incoming content can be persisted without a valid owning app. Add the apps.id reference in the schema and migration, create real app fixtures, and verify that nonexistent app ownership is rejected.
findings.title: Not done: app foreign key in the inbox schema
